::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 28th [1893?]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS West Devon Area Record Office Acc No 308
:::

My dear [Mary](people/person_1626.qmd)
I was obliged to let the [Guardian](organizations/other_75.qmd) go that week before I had really read it, but it must be a mistake for our dear [Charles](people/person_1601.qmd) cannot be referred to in Bp Wordsworths [Christian Boyhood](other_books/otherbook_677.qmd), as it was published before his death.[^1]  I know he had a copy full of marks of his own.  There is a note in the book about the poet Bowles and the habits at [Winchester](organizations/other_50.qmd), and I think the letter writer must have confused this with the great influence that Charles certainly had for I do not believe there is any tablet.  We must have known of it if one had been put up.  I was at Domum this week and had a glimpse of [Edmund](people/person_42.qmd) but not of [Geoffrey](people/person_1609.qmd).[^2] I think I never came across so few people that I knew partly because it was crowded, and partly because it was dark.  But two of the married Moberly daughters were there and I walked about with them, and felt like old times, though one of them ([Kitty Barter](people/person_114.qmd)) had a tall handsome daughter of eighteen with her. I am glad [Frances](people/person_1605.qmd) is so much better  I hope all her troubles will be over while the warm weather lasts, but she will have to take care in the winter -  I think Doctors always dislike one going to Church.  [Gertrude](people/person_1462.qmd) is on the whole better, she has been spending a week in my room instead of her own while there was a chimney sweeping and cleaning – her first change for ten months!  Today she is gone back again.  That unfortunate [Mrs F Yonge](people/person_2127.qmd) has been applying to [Colonel Oldfield](people/person_2128.qmd)who wrote to [John Eyre Yonge](people/person_1620.qmd)about her. [^3] She seems to be in a hopeless state of illness by his account (John’s) but he fancies it is a first application.  One son is in the post office, getting 10s a week.  Fancy Morgan [?] having a brother with such young children!  [Mr Coward](people/person_2129.qmd)(our locum tenens) is very young 27 & looking younger.  He has a splendid voice -  On St James’s day, at evening service when we don’t have the choir or any singing, he gave out a hymn, and while we were gazing in amazement sang it all right through by himself!

your most affectionate cousin
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Mary's brother Edmund Charles Yonge (1827-1847).  Charles Wordsworth (1806-1892), a master at Winchester before he became Bishop of St Andrews, had published *Christian Boyhood at a Public School: A Collection of Sermons and Lectures Delivered at Winchester College*  2 vols (London: Francis 1846).
[^2]: Mary’s nephews.  Geoffrey Yonge (1867-1893) had perhaps come down to Domum as an old boy of Winchester College;  Edmund Anderson Morshead (1849-1912) was a master there.
[^3]: The most likely Mrs F. Yonge seems to be Mary (Jones) Yonge, the indigent widow of Dr John Francis Duke Yonge (1814-1879), son of CMY’s uncle the Rev. Duke Yonge, Vicar of Antony.  Colonel Oldfield was the stepson of his sister Delia (Yonge) Oldfield (1807-1864).  However, the reference to 'Morgan' is obscure.
